finding: For any k>=2 and m<=2k-2 distinct positive nodes with nonzero coefficient pairs whose products have alternating signs, the corresponding m-by-2k alternating-moment matrix has full row rank and a strictly positive kernel vector. This excludes a linear-tangency-only negative certificate for the unrestricted numerator, uniformly over all derivative magnitudes and without a numerator profile. The proof combines a weak four-or-k-moment sign-variation lemma, a combined-sign-change bound through skipped zero multipliers, and finite-dimensional separation. Applied to the physical five-contact septic parity-band ordering, it gives a strictly positive-coefficient exact-degree-seven polynomial satisfying all five necessary contact tangencies. A rational seven-node abstract example has a strictly positive dual vector and shows the six-node threshold sharp for k=4; it is not asserted to be an actual interval box.
